additionalCoursework:
Coursework requirements are met through competency demonstration. Applicants must meet 9 out of 11 competencies to move forward in the admissions process. Any combination of 9 competencies are accepted; no one competency is required or privileged above others. All 11 competencies are listed in full above in the Admissions Policies & Information section of the MSAR, as well as on our website at https://medicine.illinois.edu/admissions/before-you-apply . 

Competencies using online courses outside of a transcripted college or university course will be reviewed by faculty; these courses must have an element of assessment, and faculty may judge any course to be insufficient to meet competency depending on its content and level of coverage.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
At Carle Illinois College of Medicine (CI MED), we are committed to cultivating an inclusive environment where students, faculty, and staff can learn, teach, innovate, serve, and thrive. The Office of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion advances this mission by fostering belonging through intentional programming, community partnerships, and equity-centered initiatives.
Beyond the classroom, CI MED students actively engage in experiential learning opportunities that deepen their understanding of community needs and empower them to respond through meaningful, service-driven engagement. These initiatives reflect our commitment to inclusive excellence and health innovation.
Examples of recent student-led and community-engaged programming can be found here:
https://medicine.illinois.edu/diversity/student-events

medSchoolStudLife.setting: Champaign-Urbana is a micro-urban community known for its big-city amenities yet small-town affordability, accessibility, safety, and friendliness. The twin cities are dynamic and vibrant, with a lively cultural scene, a variety of restaurants, and numerous recreational opportunities. Hailed by Midwest Living as a “Great Midwest Food Town,” Champaign-Urbana is a foodie’s paradise. It also boasts an assortment of shopping, coffee houses, clubs, live music venues, movie theaters and athletic events. A major center for the arts, the University of Illinois attracts dozens of internationally renowned artists each year to more than 350 performances held at the widely acclaimed Krannert Center for the Performing Arts. The state-of-the-art Activities and Recreation Center is one of the premier campus recreation facilities in the country. Champaign and Urbana have many award-winning park facilities and programs with popular sports leagues.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Whether you’re looking for a quiet tree-lined neighborhood or the bustle of a larger apartment complex, you’ll find an array of affordable options in Champaign-Urbana. The average monthly rent for a two-bedroom apartment is $1405. While off-campus housing is most popular, there are a limited number of graduate and family housing units available. Champaign-Urbana’s award-winning mass transit bus system covers the majority of the twin cities and is free to students. With a convenient schedule to and from Carle Illinois facilities, it’s a great option and very popular. Pedestrian-friendly and bike-friendly, Champaign-Urbana has a growing number of bike lanes on shared roads. Each MTD bus is also equipped with an easy-to-use bike rack. Uber, Lyft and Zipcar are also available.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Office of Student Affairs and the Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion provides support to all students, including gender and sexual minority students.  
Student interest groups such as Carle Pride and the Women’s Health Interest Group are supported through the Offices of Student Affairs and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.  Carle Pride creates a support network for LGBTQ+ identifying and allied medical students and prepare individuals to provide LGBTQ+ inclusive care to patients. Women's Health Interest Group creates a space to learn about women's health and educating on current standards of care, research, and policies that aim to better the lives and health of women. UIUC Counseling Center offers support groups for LGBTQ+ students.  The Gender and Sexuality Resource Center offers educational and social programs that foster an environment that is open, welcoming and safe for all identities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Disability Resources and Educational Services (DRES) ensures that qualified individuals with disabilities are afforded an equal opportunity to participate in and benefit from the programs, services, and activities of UIUC through the identification and enactment of reasonable modifications to institutional policies and procedures, the provision of effective auxiliary aids and services, and the establishment of innovative educational services. The CI MED liaison to DRES works directly with students to facilitate the process of accessing reasonable accommodations for qualifying disabilities.  Students requiring accommodation for USMLE Step exams receive referrals for diagnostic services, support with navigating the timeline and process for approval and implementation of accommodations.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Thrive is a weekly wellness series designed to address all domains of student wellness.  Sessions feature invited speakers who share valuable resources and evidenced-based wellness strategies to support them throughout medical school and their journey toward a physician-innovator career.  Lunch is provided for students at Thrive sessions. 

The Carle Illinois College of Medicine Wellness Mentoring Program is a peer-to-peer initiative designed to support first-year medical students as they transition into medical school, fostering both personal and professional growth through mentoring and meaningful interpersonal connections.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Carle Illinois’ curriculum immerses students early in clinical, case-driven, problem-based active learning intended to instill passion and creativity for discovering innovative solutions to the world’s most difficult healthcare challenges. As such, we work hard to maintain a collaborative, team-focused culture to exemplify our values of compassion, creativity, curiosity, diversity, and collaboration.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students are expected to maintain reliable transportation for clinical experiences that will occur up to one hour outside of the Champaign-Urbana area. We highly recommend that students have a car because rural areas are not reliably covered by public transportation and rideshare agencies. Clinical experiences will begin as early as week 3 of the curriculum, and students are responsible for their travel regardless of site placement. Site placement map: https://go.medicine.illinois.edu/SitesMap

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Carle Illinois College of Medicine is the first college of medicine designed at the intersection of medicine and engineering. Balancing clinical medicine and biosciences with engineering and the humanities centers our work on the human condition. Carle Illinois students will drive innovations through engineering rounds, projects, publications, inventions, and commercialization. Our case-driven, problem-based, active learning curriculum at the nexus of engineering, biology, and medicine is systems-based and patient-centered, incorporating early clinical exposure with an innovation and research focus. Our vision is to enable better healthcare for more people at lower cost by catalyzing transformative research at the intersection of engineering, basic science, and human health.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Carle Illinois is dedicated to the development of clinical skills across all specialties. We expose our students to primary care beginning in week 2 of the curriculum. During the first year, students spend one afternoon weekly in a primary care practice. In year 2, our students begin a unique longitudinal experience in the Family Medicine Continuity Clinic Course, seeing their own panel of patients alongside a team of other students and a preceptor for 18 months. In addition to other core clerkships, Carle Illinois now has a dedicated 5-week Family Medicine Clerkship where students work with Family Medicine physicians in a patient-centered medical home to round out their experience in primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Carle Illinois students work hand-in-hand with world-class researchers to receive high-touch guidance and mentorship during their training. As students encounter healthcare’s greatest challenges, they bring their ideas to the lab, work closely with Research Mentors, and develop high-impact solutions for the world. The Health Maker Lab at Illinois is a network of fabrication labs where the only limit to harnessing technology to improve human health is your imagination. Carle Illinois students will bring their ideas to life by engineering new solutions to global health challenges through forward design and synthesis of frontier molecules, cells, tissues and systems that translate to improving human health and well-being.

More information on Carle Illinois' research opportunities can be found at: https://medicine.illinois.edu/research/
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: You will work in small teams alongside experts in medicine, engineering and science to tackle real-life cases with an interdisciplinary approach that is uniquely Illinois.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
A partnership between the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) and Carle Health, Carle Illinois College of Medicine educates physician innovators to revolutionize the way health care is delivered, leveraging technology and data to improve patient care and outcomes.

The curriculum is built at the intersection of engineering and medicine, with most courses designed by a basic scientist, clinician, and engineer. Students are immersed in case-driven, problem-based learning. 

High value is placed on patient-centered care, systems-based delivery, innovation and research, and early clinical exposure. The curriculum infuses basic sciences, clinical sciences, engineering and innovation, and medical humanities into all four years. Innovation is the cornerstone, with emphasis on human factors, design thinking, and entrepreneurship. 

Carle Illinois draws on the contributions of physicians and researchers from across the UIUC/Carle enterprise to deliver a world-class medical education.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The Carle Illinois College of Medicine is the world’s first engineering-based medical school. 

We educate exceptional physician-innovators to deliver high-value, compassionate health care through transformative solutions developed at the intersection of engineering, science and medicine. A CI MED physician innovator will be a leader who is trained via interdisciplinary immersion to develop these transformative health care solutions.

Our vision is to be a global leader in transformative medical education, research and clinical care innovation, improving the health and well-being of patients and communities around the world.

We are driven by key qualities that permeate our culture and result in a self-enhancing environment:

•	Compassion: We are focused on improving the human condition through compassionate care for patients, society and the world at large.

•	Competence: We are confident in our capacity to prepare board-certified physicians who are also innovators who will revolutionize healthcare delivery.

•	Curiosity: Change doesn’t just happen. Through a unique blend of unwavering curiosity, determination and a giant leap into new ways of thinking, we challenge the status quo.

•	Creativity: We will develop unprecedented solutions to society’s most challenging healthcare delivery problems by collectively building on each other’s creative ideas.

•	Collaboration: We leverage our strategic partnerships with Carle Health, the University of Illinois. and the community to enhance our innovative curriculum, expand learning opportunities, and advance human health.

•	Diversity: We actively promote an inclusive environment in which students, faculty, and staff can learn, teach, research, and serve.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All applicants are required to submit letters of evaluation and recommendation, and all letters of evaluation and recommendation must be submitted to AMCAS letter service. Carle Illinois College of Medicine Admissions Committee will accept at least three but no more than four letters of evaluation. Applicants submitting a premedical committee report or other composite letter of recommendation may submit one additional letter of recommendation. Any letters from third parties that are not solicited by the applicant or Carle Illinois College of Medicine or letters sent directly to Carle Illinois College of Medicine will not be accepted or retained and do not become a part of the applicant’s file for consideration by the Admissions Committee.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants are advised to choose a group of letter writers that can collectively speak to their:
•	Skill in STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts and Mathematics)
•	Work ethic and engagement
•	Leadership and teamwork
•	Potential to be a successful innovator
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Carle Illinois College of Medicine does not conduct interviews. Finalist evaluation generally begins mid-fall, and offers do not typically go out until the following January.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Education
All applicants are required to have earned a degree at the Bachelor’s level or higher from an accredited U.S. or Canadian  college or university prior to matriculation in the MD Program. No single major is preferred.

Academic Requirements: MCAT and GPA
Applicants must complete the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) prior to application consideration. 
Both MCAT and GPA will be used as components in a holistic evaluation of an applicant. For the MCAT, we require a minimum total score of 498 out of a possible 528. MCAT scores must not be more than 3 years old in January of the year of expected enrollment. The best valid score will be used for the admission process. We do not have a minimum GPA requirement.
 
Required Competency Areas
Applicants must demonstrate competency in at least 9 of 11 competency areas listed below to receive a secondary application. Competency most likely will be met through courses taken during undergraduate education. Community college credit is accepted. Advanced Placement credit is ONLY accepted when succeeded by a higher-level course in the same subject at an undergraduate institution.

The competency areas and coursework that could demonstrate adequate competency:
1. chemistry -- 3 semesters or equivalent of general and/or organic chemistry with lab
2. biochemistry -- 1 semester or equivalent
3. biology -- 2 semesters or equivalent with lab
4. advanced biology -- 1 semester or equivalent of physiology, systems biology, or other advanced biology course
5. physics -- 2 semesters or equivalent with lab
6. humanities / social sciences -- as required by undergraduate major
7. statistics -- 1 semester or equivalent
8. calculus -- 2 semesters or equivalent; content of higher-level class should be comparable to UIUC MATH 231 (Calculus II)
9. multivariate calculus -- Content of class should be comparable to UIUC MATH 241 (Calculus III); see https://medicine.illinois.edu/admissions/faq/  
10. differential equations -- Content of class should be comparable to UIUC MATH 285 (Intro to Differential Equations); see https://medicine.illinois.edu/admissions/faq/  
11. linear algebra -- Content of class should be comparable to UIUC MATH 415 (Applied Linear Algebra); see https://medicine.illinois.edu/admissions/faq/  

We recognize there are alternatives to undergraduate coursework that may prepare you for our curriculum. These may include, but are not limited to, research publications, professional experiences, or certificates. You will have the opportunity to provide documentation of alternative experiences that demonstrate competence. To see how the University of Illinois interprets your prior coursework, please refer to Transferology or speak to the pre-health advisor from your college/university. Regretfully, due to a high volume of requests, we are unable to provide individual pre-application assessments. Applications must be submitted through AMCAS, and will undergo a thorough, holistic evaluation to ensure that applicants have the appropriate competencies to succeed in our unique curriculum.

Suggested Experience
Carle Illinois College of Medicine is committed to the use of holistic admissions to identify applicants who are best suited to our institutional mission and educational design. In addition to strong interpersonal skills, demonstrated altruism, leadership skills, experience in healthcare settings, and strong preparation in pre-med plus quantitative areas, applicants with experience coding, participating in research studies, working directly with patients as an EMT or medical assistant, or working in industry have found success in our curriculum and excelled outside of the classroom.

Citizenship
-Currently, only U.S. citizens or permanent residents will be considered.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Institutional loans are not available to students in the Carle Illinois College of Medicine. Students who file the FAFSA, using our school code of 001775, will be considered for Federal Unsubsidized loan options. Students have the option of securing loans through private sources, if additional funding is needed. Additional information is available at: http://www.osfa.illinois.edu/types-of-aid/alternative-educational-loans.

All admitted students are automatically considered for scholarships.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Carle Illinois considers all previous coursework, regardless of the date the coursework was completed.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Holistic evaluation is used to ensure applicants are ready to succeed in our unique curriculum. In addition, through our secondary application, we want to get to know our applicants. We're looking for physician-innovators; and in leading by example, we are offering an innovative, non-traditional secondary application process. We ask applicants to show us how they are prepared for our unique curriculum, built at the intersection of engineering and medicine.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We subscribe to the AAMC's holistic review process and feel that shadowing helps demonstrate readiness for medical school. While shadowing experience is not required, we feel that experience in a clinical setting can strengthen an application.
